svg.title: 4. Upgrade playbook: 1.34 to 1.35
svg.text: Watch the SLOs, not the nodes
What blocked the prod drain for 40 minutes
When to build a new cluster instead (blue/green)
Scenario: upgrading the shared cluster from Kubernetes 1.34 to 1.35 before standard support ends (2 Dec 2026)
deprecated API calls seen in the
Found: 2 Helm charts on an old API.
and every add-on to versions that
One minor version at a time,
updated one by one, each with
of DNS errors and pod starts.
Every node is marked Drifted and
cordon and drain the old one.
Tag the Git release, write down
14 nodes would not drain. Each ran a pod of loyalty-sync: 1 replica with a
PodDisruptionBudget of minAvailable: 1. Zero evictions allowed, so Karpenter
Fix on the day: the team scaled loyalty-sync to 2 replicas; the drain finished.
- Kyverno rule: a PDB is only accepted if the workload has 2+ replicas
- terminationGracePeriod on every NodePool as a hard backstop
- a "drain-blockers" panel in Grafana, checked before every upgrade
In-place is the default: it keeps the IPs, the load balancers, the Lattice
associations and the 7-day rollback. Build a second cluster and move
traffic over (weighted DNS or ALB target groups) when:
- you are more than one minor version behind and cannot step through
- you are changing something set at creation: IPv6, service CIDR
- the cluster carries years of hand-made drift nobody can explain
- a stateful system needs a rehearsed, reversible cut-over
It costs a second control plane and a second set of nodes for days.
